card.name: Be after may/should in recommendations
card.fires_on: The word "be" right after "may" or "should" (occasionally "may" itself) in label sentences about tests, monitoring or adjustments. It is strongest after a subject like "testing" or "determinations".

modes.label: Be after testing noun
modes.description: "be" follows "may" or "should" after a lab or evaluation noun, leading to "performed" or "necessary".
modes.example: Hepatic laboratory testing should<< be>> performed in patients with underlying liver disease prior

modes.label: May after a drug name
modes.description: "may" follows a drug name in an interaction statement.
modes.example: Eslicarbazepine acetate tablets<< may>> decrease the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives

card.writes: It seems to push toward passive formal phrasing such as "this kind of" or "can then", though the output tokens are mostly uninformative.
card.plain: It fires on the "be" in "should be performed" or "may be necessary" in label advice about tests and monitoring.
